chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'What is your view of the deceased when he dies, why is the twig placed with him?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Punishment and Reckoning are staved off from him as long as the wood is wet.'

He (peace be upon him) said: 'And all the punishment is in one day, in one hour, the measure of what it takes to enter the grave and for the people to return. And the two fronds were made for that purpose, so no punishment or reckoning befalls him after they dry up, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.السَّعَفَتَانِ: The two fronds (of the date palm twig)

ai.seo_question: Why is a twig placed with the deceased in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the 'jarida' (twig) serves as a physical signifier for the duration of the initial phase of grave punishment, which is compressed into a single hour equivalent to the time of burial and return. This highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that while the soul undergoes immediate reckoning, the physical decay of the twig correlates with the mitigation or completion of this specific punitive interval, offering a tangible link between the material world and the barzakh state.
